subject: Numerical Methods
chapters: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations

questions.text: Explain errors in numerical computation: Round-off error, Truncation error, Absolute error, Relative error, and Percentage error. Discuss the significance of significant digits in scientific computation.
If a true value $X = 0.006897$ is truncated to three decimal digits, calculate the absolute error, relative error, and percentage error.
If $x = 1.350253$ is rounded off to four significant digits, calculate the absolute error and relative error.
Explain the principle and working mechanism of the Bisection Method. Write an algorithm and pseudo-code to find a real root of a non-linear equation.
Use the Bisection method to find a positive real root of $x^3 - 2x - 5 = 0$ correct up to 4 decimal places.
Use the Bisection method to find a positive real root of $\sin x - \frac{1}{x} = 0$ or $x^3 - 4x - 9 = 0$ correct up to three decimal places.
Derive the Newton-Raphson iterative formula $x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$ using Taylor series expansion. Explain its rate of convergence (quadratic convergence).
Use the Newton-Raphson method to find a positive real root of $x e^x - 1 = 0$ or $\sin x + \cos x + e^x - 8 = 0$ correct to 4 decimal places.
Find the reciprocal of $3$ (or $\sqrt{N}$) using the Newton-Raphson method correct up to 4 decimal places.
Explain the Secant Method and False Position (Regula-Falsi) Method. Differentiate between them with geometric sketches and write an algorithm for the Secant method.
Calculate the real root of non-linear equation $f(x) = \sin x - 2x + 1 = 0$ or $f(x) = x^3 - \cos x = 0$ using the Secant method with absolute error less than $10^{-3}$.

State and prove the condition for convergence of the Fixed Point Iteration method $|g'(x)| < 1$. Discuss the limitations of fixed-point iteration graphically and solve $x^3 + x^2 - 3 = 0$ correct to four decimal places.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Explain Gauss Elimination Method with Partial Pivoting. Write an algorithm and pseudo-code to solve a system of $N$ linear algebraic equations.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Solve the following system of linear equations using Gauss Elimination with Partial Pivoting: $2x + 3y + 2z = 2$ $10x + 3y + 4z = 16$ $3x + 6y + z = 6$

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Solve the following linear system using Gauss Elimination method: $x + 2y + 3z = 6$ $2x + 3y + 5z = 10$ $2x - y + 3z = 4$

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Explain the Gauss-Jordan Method for solving linear systems and finding the inverse of a square matrix. Write a Python/C program to solve linear equations using Gauss-Jordan.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Find the inverse of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$ using the Gauss-Jordan elimination method.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Explain Gauss-Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel Iterative methods. State the condition for diagonal dominance: $|a_{ii}| > \sum_{j \ne i} |a_{ij}|$. Why does Gauss-Seidel converge faster than Gauss-Jacobi?

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Solve the following system using Gauss-Seidel iteration method (perform 3 iterations): $8x + 2y - 2z = 8$ $x - 8y + 3z = -4$ $2x + y + 9z = 12$

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Explain the Power Method to determine the dominant (largest) eigenvalue and corresponding eigenvector of a square matrix. Write an algorithm and pseudo-code.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Find the dominant eigenvalue and corresponding eigenvector of matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ using the Power Method with an accuracy of 2 decimal places.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Solution of System of Linear Algebraic Equations
questions.text: Find the largest eigenvalue and corresponding eigenvector of matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ using the Power Method.
Derive Newton's Forward Difference Interpolation formula and construct the forward difference table from given equally spaced data.
Derive Newton's Backward Difference Interpolation formula and explain when it is preferred over forward interpolation.
From the following table, estimate $f(1.6)$ and $f(3.25)$ using Newton's forward interpolation method: $x: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ $f(x): 1, 4, 9, 16, 25$
Derive Lagrange's Interpolation formula for unequally spaced data. Write a C program to numerically interpolate a value from a given data set using Lagrange's formula.
Using Lagrange's interpolation formula, find the value of $f(1.3)$ from data: $(1, 1), (2, 4), (4, 16), (5, 25)$.
Derive Newton's Divided Difference Interpolation formula. Construct divided difference table and approximate the value of $y(9)$ from data: $(2, 4), (4, 56), (6, 204), (8, 496), (10, 980)$.
Explain Natural Cubic Spline Interpolation technique. State the boundary conditions for clamped vs natural splines. From data $(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5)$, estimate $y(2.5)$.
Explain the Method of Least Squares for curve fitting. Derive normal equations to fit a linear straight line $y = a x + b$ to a set of $N$ experimental data points.
Use the method of least squares to fit a second-degree polynomial (parabola) $y = a x^2 + b x + c$ to the data: $(-3, 12), (-1, 2), (1, 0), (3, 6)$.
Fit an exponential curve of the form $y = a e^{b x}$ to the given data: $(1, 1.2), (2, 2.8), (3, 6.5), (4, 15.1)$ using the least squares method.
Fit a power curve of the form $y = a x^b$ or $y = a b^x$ to experimental observations using the least squares method.
Fit a logarithmic curve of the form $y = a \ln x + b$ to experimental observations using the least squares method and estimate $y(15)$.
Derive expressions for numerical differentiation to evaluate the first derivative $y'(x)$ and second derivative $y''(x)$ using Newton's forward difference formula.
Derive expressions to evaluate the first and second derivatives from Newton's backward difference formula.

The distances $s$ (km) traveled by a vehicle at intervals of $t = 2\text{ minutes}$ are: $(2, 0.25), (4, 1.0), (6, 2.2), (8, 4.0), (10, 6.5), (12, 8.5)$. Evaluate the velocity and acceleration of the vehicle at $t = 3\text{ minutes}$.

A rod is rotating in a plane. The angular displacement $\theta$ (radians) at time $t$ (seconds) is given by: $(0, 0), (0.2, 0.12), (0.4, 0.49), (0.6, 1.10), (0.8, 2.01)$. Calculate the angular velocity and angular acceleration of the rod at $t = 0.2\text{ s}$ and $t = 0.6\text{ s}$.
Derive the Newton-Cotes general quadrature formula for numerical integration and deduce the Trapezoidal Rule and Composite Trapezoidal Rule.

Derive Simpson's 1/3 Rule and Composite Simpson's 1/3 Rule for numerical integration. State its degree of precision and error term. Evaluate $\int_0^1 \frac{1}{1 + x^2} dx$ taking $h = 0.25$ and compare with analytical value.
Derive Composite Simpson's 3/8 Rule for integration. Evaluate $\int_0^2 (e^x + \sin 2x) dx$ with step size $h = 0.4$.

Explain Romberg Integration method using Richardson extrapolation formula $I(h_1, h_2) = \frac{4 I(h_2) - I(h_1)}{3}$. Evaluate $\int_{-1}^1 e^x \sin x dx$ to 3 decimal places taking initial step-size $h = (b-a)/2$.

Explain Gaussian Quadrature. Derive Gauss-Legendre 2-point and 3-point quadrature formulas with weights and abscissas. Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi} (\sin x + \cos x) dx$ or $\int_0^1 e^{-x^2} dx$ using Gauss-Legendre 3-point formula.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain Euler's Method and Modified Euler's (Heun's) Method for solving initial value problems (IVP) $\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y), y(x_0) = y_0$. Write an algorithm and pseudo-code. Solve $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sin x + \cos y, y(0) = 1$ in $0 \le x \le 1$ with step size $h = 0.2$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain Runge-Kutta 2nd Order (RK-2) method (Heun's form, Midpoint form, Ralston's form). Solve $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sin x + \cos x - y, y(0) = 1$ for $x = 0.2$ using RK-2.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain Classical Runge-Kutta 4th Order (RK-4) method. Write a high-level language program (C/C++) to solve first-order differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sin(nx) + \cos(y), y(0) = 2$ in range $0 \le x \le 1$ with step-size $h = 0.5$ using RK-4.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain how higher-order ordinary differential equations and systems of simultaneous ODEs are solved using the RK-4 method. Write pseudo-code to solve $y'' + x y' + y = 0, y(0) = 1, y'(0) = 0$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain the Shooting Method for solving two-point boundary value problems (BVP). Use shooting method employing Euler's formula with step-size $h = 0.5$ to solve $y'' = 0.5x - y + y' + 3$ with boundary conditions $y(0) = 5, y(2) = 8$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Explain Finite Difference Method for solving Boundary Value Problems. Discretize $y'' + 2y' - y = x$ subject to $y(0) = 1.5, y(2) = 2.5$ by dividing the interval into 4 sub-intervals ($h = 0.5$) and solve the resulting linear system.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
questions.text: Solve boundary value problem $y'' + 4y' - 3y = \sin x$ with boundary conditions $y(0) = 3, y(4) = 4$ for three interior points using the finite difference approximation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: Solve Laplace's Equation $\nabla^2 u = \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 0$ on a square plate of size $8\text{ cm} \times 8\text{ cm}$ with grid size $2\text{ cm} \times 2\text{ cm}$. Boundary values are $50$ on top side, $30$ on bottom side, and $10$ on left and right sides. Formulate the system of finite difference equations and compute steady-state temperature at interior nodes.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: A metal sheet of size $30\text{ cm} \times 30\text{ cm}$ has two adjacent sides maintained at $50^\circ\text{C}$ and other two sides at $500^\circ\text{C}$. Calculate steady-state temperature at interior grid points using grid size $10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}$ using the standard 5-point finite difference formula.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: Explain Finite Difference Scheme for Poisson's Equation $\nabla^2 u = f(x, y)$. Solve $u_{xx} + u_{yy} = -81xy$ over square domain $0 < x < 1, 0 < y < 1$ with step size $h = 1/3$ and boundary conditions $u(0, y) = u(x, 0) = 0$ and $u(1, y) = u(x, 1) = 100$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: Solve Poisson's equation $u_{xx} + u_{yy} = 243(x^3 + y^3)$ over the square domain $0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1$ with step size $h = 1/3$ with $u = 100$ on the boundary.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: Derive the Bender-Schmidt explicit recurrence formula for solving the 1D Heat Conduction Equation $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}$. State the stability condition $\lambda = \frac{c^2 k}{h^2} \le \frac{1}{2}$. Solve boundary value problem $u_t = u_{xx}$ with $u(0, t) = u(1, t) = 0$ and $u(x, 0) = \sin(\pi x)$ up to $t = 5\text{ seconds}$ with $h = 0.2$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Solution of Partial Differential Equations
questions.text: Explain the Crank-Nicolson implicit method for solving the 1D heat equation. Why is it unconditionally stable compared to the Bender-Schmidt explicit method?
